payload.notes: Round 1 of the Tidemark mark: six directions on one idea, **the line the water leaves**. Look at which still reads at 16 px and in the one-colour menu bar, and which sits best beside the wordmark.

marks.name: Three waves
marks.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><rect x="3" y="6" width="18" height="3" rx="1.5" fill="var(--accent)" /><rect x="5" y="11" width="14" height="3" rx="1.5" fill="currentColor" /><rect x="7" y="16" width="10" height="3" rx="1.5" fill="currentColor" /></svg>
marks.reasoning: Three bars that shorten as the tide goes out, the highest in the accent: the mark the water left. Reads as a stack at 16 px, which is the risk.

marks.name: High-water ring
marks.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8.5" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.4" /><rect x="2" y="10.8" width="20" height="2.4" rx="1.2" fill="var(--accent)" /></svg>
marks.reasoning: A ring with the waterline through it, like a gauge seen head on. The simplest cut, and the one most like a hundred other marks.

marks.name: The notch
marks.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M4 4h16v16H4z M4 11h6l2 2l2 -2h6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.4" stroke-linejoin="round" /><rect x="10.8" y="11" width="2.4" height="3" fill="var(--accent)" /></svg>
marks.reasoning: A square cut by a line with a notch where the level was read. Clever at 128 px; the notch closes up below 24.

marks.name: Post and line
marks.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><rect x="4" y="3" width="3" height="18" rx="1.5" fill="currentColor" /><rect x="17" y="3" width="3" height="18" rx="1.5" fill="currentColor" /><rect x="7" y="10.5" width="10" height="3" rx="1.5" fill="var(--accent)" /></svg>
marks.reasoning: Two posts with the level strung between them. The fewest parts and the most legible at 16 px; the accent carries the idea on its own.

marks.name: Tide gauge
marks.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><rect x="10.5" y="2" width="3" height="20" rx="1.5" fill="currentColor" /><rect x="6" y="5" width="4" height="2" rx="1" fill="currentColor" /><rect x="6" y="11" width="4" height="2" rx="1" fill="currentColor" /><rect x="6" y="17" width="4" height="2" rx="1" fill="currentColor" /><rect x="14" y="13" width="6" height="3" rx="1.5" fill="var(--accent)" /></svg>
marks.reasoning: A staff with its ticks and the reading beside it. Honest about what the product does; busy in the menu bar.

marks.name: The drop
marks.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M12 3c3.5 4.5 6 7.8 6 11a6 6 0 0 1 -12 0c0 -3.2 2.5 -6.5 6 -11z" fill="currentColor" /><rect x="6.5" y="14" width="11" height="2.4" rx="1.2" fill="var(--accent)" /></svg>
marks.reasoning: A drop with the line across it. Warm and readable at every size, but it says water more than it says change.
